scenes.audio: Elena owns Universal Life coverage and wants to reduce her payments while changing jobs. Universal Life separates premium funding, interest credits, and policy deductions.
scenes.label: Opening Hook
scenes.visual: A man and a woman are seated at a dark wood kitchen table. The man, in his early 40s with a dark complexion, short black hair, and a groomed beard, wears a navy blue button-down shirt. He leans over an open silver laptop. The woman, in her late 30s with a tanned complexion and long dark wavy hair, wears an olive green button-down shirt. She holds a white document, pointing at it while they both focus on the paper. The background is a brightly lit, modern kitchen with white cabinetry and large windows providing soft natural light. A ceramic mug sits in the foreground.

scenes.audio: The owner may have flexibility within the contract, but insurance costs and administrative charges continue.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Transition to a static graphic on a pale cream background. A single white rectangular box with a numerical label in the top left corner appears on the left. A green arrow points horizontally from this box toward the center of the frame.

scenes.audio: A planned premium is not automatically the amount guaranteed to sustain coverage forever. If payments and earnings do not support the deductions, the available value can decline.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: A second dark teal rectangular box appears in the center of the frame, next to the first one. Another green arrow points from the center box to the right side of the frame.

scenes.audio: Without an applicable protection provision, insufficient funding can lead to lapse after the required process.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: A third white rectangular box appears on the right side of the frame, completing a horizontal row of three elements. The background remains a flat, pale cream color with consistent lighting.

scenes.audio: First, read the policy's funding conditions and current statement, then discuss the effect of the proposed change.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: The three boxes remain static on the screen. The layout is balanced and centered.

scenes.audio: Use a deliberately simplified teaching account. It begins with $1,000. A $200 payment adds $190 after an assumed $10 premium charge.
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: The screen cuts to a new graphic layout on a pale cream background. A large white rectangular box appears on the left containing mathematical figures and symbols. The lighting is uniform and artificial.

scenes.audio: Assume $20 of interest is credited and $130 of insurance and other charges are deducted. The ending value is $1,080.
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: A second white rectangular box appears to the right of the first, containing additional mathematical symbols and figures.

scenes.audio: Now remove the payment while keeping the other assumptions fixed. The ending value becomes $890.
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: The existing boxes shift slightly as new numerical values appear below the original ones to represent a secondary scenario.

scenes.audio: This example illustrates separate flows, not a real carrier's calculation order or guaranteed monthly return. Missing a payment does not make the insurance charges disappear.
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: The static graphic remains on screen, displaying two sets of comparative numerical calculations.

scenes.audio: Interest-sensitive and current assumption designs respond to the pricing and crediting terms stated in the contract.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Transition to a three-column graphic layout. On the far left, a white box with a blue header appears. The background is consistent with previous scenes.

scenes.audio: An indeterminate premium whole life design may change its current premium within a guaranteed maximum.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: A second column with a green header appears in the center of the frame.

scenes.audio: Universal life instead presents flexible funding and separately identified charges and credits. Do not treat those structures as identical. The insurer's current credited rate or illustrated performance may differ from the contractual minimum.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: A third column with a pale yellow header appears on the far right.

scenes.audio: Rising insurance costs or lower earnings can affect the funding needed. A no-lapse guarantee, when included, has its own required payment pattern, period, and conditions.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: The three-column graphic remains static, showing three distinct sections of information.

scenes.audio: Indexed life links a credited interest calculation to a named external index under the policy's rules.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Cut to a new graphic showing a numbered list. The first item appears at the top left with a teal label. The background is pale cream.

scenes.audio: An indexed universal life policy does not directly invest the owner's policy value in that stock index. A participation rate determines the share of the stated index change used.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: A second numbered item appears below the first one. The design is clean and minimalist.

scenes.audio: A cap limits the credited rate while a spread can reduce the rate under a different stated formula. A floor provides the stated minimum for that crediting calculation.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Third and fourth numbered items appear sequentially down the left side of the screen.

scenes.audio: Methods and available rates differ by contract and strategy. Do not present the index's headline return as the policy's actual return or assume that stock dividends are included.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: The full list of four numbered items is displayed on the screen.

scenes.audio: Assume a teaching strategy uses an 8% positive index change, 75% participation, a 5% cap, and a 0% floor with no spread.
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: Cut to a graphic containing three white rectangular boxes arranged horizontally. The first box on the left contains mathematical equations.

scenes.audio: Participation produces 6%. The cap reduces the credited rate to 5%.
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: The center box populates with a calculation result involving a percentage limit.

scenes.audio: Under the same strategy, a negative index change would produce 0% interest because of the floor.
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: The third box on the right populates with final notes regarding deductions and returns.

scenes.audio: These are illustrative assumptions, not currently offered rates. Policy charges still apply. Zero index interest can accompany a falling policy value after deductions.
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: The three-box graphic remains static, showing the comparative results of the mathematical demonstration.

scenes.audio: Elena should review the death benefit option, current account and surrender values, deductions, premium history, and any guarantee's status.
scenes.label: Real Experience
scenes.visual: Return to the scene of the man and woman from the start of the video. They are still at the kitchen table, looking at the same document. The woman nods slightly, and the man remains focused on the paper. The lighting and environment are identical to the first scene.

scenes.audio: Some universal designs offer a level benefit while others add the account value to a stated amount. Use the actual option and policy rules.
scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.visual: Transition to a final graphic showing a numbered list of four items. The first item appears at the top left with a teal numerical indicator.

scenes.audio: Do not assume every policy pays both amounts. Benefit increases may require new evidence of insurability.
scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.visual: The second and third items on the list appear below the first.

scenes.audio: Request an updated in-force illustration using appropriate assumptions when reviewing future funding. Explain which figures are guaranteed and which are projections.
scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.visual: The fourth item appears at the bottom of the list, completing the graphic.

scenes.audio: A sound review connects the client's continuing protection need to an affordable funding plan and the contract's actual conditions.
scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.visual: The final graphic with all four points remains static on the screen until the end of the clip.
